items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I heard Bird when he was with Jay McShann... I caught the band and I heard it. I knew it was a new sound

ctx.x: Oh ... there was a club, not a club, but a little place, a little dancehall -- like I said, I wasn't quite 14, and I was working in this club, and it was a little dancehall right down the 30th block on Cosgrove called The Vipers. Now, it was run by an old man they called Pop Pearson and his son, Charlie. Well, Charlie had -- to me, I

believe that was the first stereo -- he made a vendor, and played records -- he had about 6 or 7 loud speakers, and he built it, and he'd sit up there and work the controls, and he knew all the arrangements, these big bands, and certain bands he would turn it up, you know, turn the volume up, and oh, it was so beautiful -- it was just like being -- sitting up close to a big band.

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I had heard about Clifford Brown, had never met him

ctx.x: Well, that was '56. The Jazz Messengers

had been in town -- I didn't catch the first, the original, group -- that was the one with Horace Mobley Donald and Hank Moby, Don Byrd, Doug Watkins, and Art Blakey Reckie -- That's the original Messengers they were the originals. They had been in, and I missed the band, and Max was working at the Beehive, and I had met Max before --back in the forties -- when he was with Bird Byrd, so Little Leo Blevins got me one night -- late one night, and said, "C'mon, Willie, let's go out and catch Max. -- -- " play some…

I had heard about Clifford Brown, had never met him -- and Malachi told me they were in the band down at Morris Brown College -- and Clifford had his first automobile accident in that college band, and spoke about it. I had heard what a great trumpet player he was, and I had hardly heard the band -- I didn't have access to no records, or recordings of the Max Roach Quintet: Clifford and Harold Land and Richie Powell and George Morrow. So I said, "Okay Leo" -- Leo wanted to get over to the club and all that ...…
